title: Terraform module version orchestrator + policy verifier pipeline for Private/VPC IaC
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Goal: Build a repeatable CI/CD pattern for Terraform modules used in Private/VPC deployment that enforces linting, policy-as-code checks, safe plan/apply automation, and integrates an automated module upgrade workflow with runtime health verification.

Background: Private customers require deterministic upgrades and safety guarantees for infra changes (security, networking). Current repo-level pipelines run ad-hoc checks but lack a unified verifier and an orchestrated module upgrade job that can safely bump module versions across multiple customer stacks. This ticket scopes a pipeline and controller (serverless or ephemeral runner) that performs: lint -> static policy eval -> plan with cost estimate -> gated apply to staging -> rollout to production with canary + health probes and automated rollback on regressions.

Design decisions & constraints:
- Keep workflows in GitHub Actions (initial phase) with a move-to-runner plan for high-scale migration.
- Use tflint + terraform validate for fast linting and basic best-practices.
- Use Conftest (rego) + OPA policies for policy-as-code enforcement. Policies will include network restrictions (no public subnets by default), encryption/KMS usage, IAM least-privilege templates, and disallowed resource types for private mode.
- Plan artifacts (JSON) must be stored as pipeline artifacts and surfaced in PR comment with a cost delta estimate.
- Module upgrades should be orchestrated via a dedicated 'module-upgrade' workflow that: creates a branch, updates module versions in pinned module sources, runs full pipeline, and opens a PR with diffs across affected stacks.
- Apply must be gated: automatic apply to staging on green; production apply requires either an explicit approval or passing automated canary verification depending on the risk tier.
- Health checks run as a post-apply job: infra health prober (VPC reachability, load-balancer status), smoke test (simple authenticated API call to service), and Terraform drift detection (periodic). Failure triggers rollback and create an incident stub.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Lint & static policy check step added to repo-level pipeline and failing PRs block merges when policy violations detected.
2) Plan artifact is generated and posted to PR with a machine-readable summary and human summary.
3) Module-upgrade workflow can automatically open PRs updating module references for at least 2 core modules (networking, instance-profiles).
4) Staging auto-apply works without human approval; production apply respects risk tier and supports canary (10% rollout) with automatic verification.
5) Health probes implemented and failure causes an automated rollback and PagerDuty alert with runbook link.
6) End-to-end integration test runs in CI demonstrating upgrade -> canary -> verify -> promote path.

Non-goals:
- Full migration to custom runners or external orchestrator (out of scope for this ticket; follow-up).
- Rewriting existing Terraform modules unless critical bugfixes are found.

Implementation tasks (high-level):
- Create Conftest rego rules for required policies and integrate into pipeline (owner: security eng).
- Add tflint config and baseline suppression list (owner: infra eng).
- Create GH Action to produce plan JSON and upload as artifact + comment summarizer action (owner: platform eng).
- Implement module-upgrade action (branch + sed/terraform get patch + open PR) with configurable module registry mapping (owner: platform eng).
- Add staged apply workflow with environment tagging and automated canary verifier job (owner: runtime eng).
- Implement health prober as a reusable script container that outputs structured probe results and returns non-zero on regression (owner: telemetry eng).
- Wire alerts to PagerDuty and Console dashboard showing last successful health check per stack (owner: observability).

Rollout plan:
1) Pilot on two non-customer staging stacks owned by Platform team.
2) Iterate on policies and probe thresholds for 1 sprint.
3) Offer opt-in for early enterprise customers; gather feedback.
4) Flip on as default for all private infra repos after 2 successful upgrades.

Risks and mitigations:
- False positive policy failures: provide an 'exceptions' registry and review flow.
- Upgrades causing latent regressions: use canary + extended smoke tests and keep fast rollback path via state snapshot.
- Secrets exposure in artifacts: redact sensitive outputs (apply plan filtering) and limit artifact TTL.

Monitoring & telemetry:
- CI metrics: policy failure rate, pipeline latency, plan-to-apply time.
- Runtime metrics: health probe pass rate, canary success rate, rollback frequency.
- Dashboards: per-repo pipeline status, per-stack last successful health check, module-version drift map.
